lines.text: Three in the morning. The nightly pipeline is running, and everyone is asleep.
Then the build fails. Red, on the main branch, with a stack trace nobody sees.
Nobody is awake, and nobody will look for hours. The broken build just sits there.
At nine, the team wakes up to a red board and a lost morning.
In Agent R Q, a failed build can emit a named event, just like a finished task does.
An event is only a name, a signal that says what happened. No code to write.
You wire that event to a fixer workspace, and it creates a task for its agent on the spot.
The fixer agent is already listening. A minute later, it picks up the task and starts.
It reads the logs, finds the failing test, and traces it to a bad import.
It opens a pull request with the fix, and does not merge it. That part is left to you.
Every workspace keeps its approvals, so a human still decides what ships.
What would you want an agent to handle while you sleep? Tell us in the comments, and try events at Agent R Q dot com.
